mcqs.question: What is the coefficient of variation (CV) in statistics?

options.A: The ratio of the standard deviation to the mean, expressed as a percentage.
options.B: The difference between the maximum and minimum values of a data set.
options.C: The square of the mean of the data set.
options.D: The sum of all observations divided by the number of observations.

mcqs.answer: The ratio of the standard deviation to the mean, expressed as a percentage.
mcqs.explanation: The coefficient of variation is defined as (standard deviation ÷ mean) × 100%, which measures relative variability. Options B, C and D describe range, a squared mean, and the mean itself, not CV.

mcqs.question: For the data set {10, 12, 14, 16, 18}, what is the coefficient of variation (rounded to one decimal place)?
mcqs.explanation: Mean = (10+12+14+16+18)/5 = 14. Variance = [(−4)²+(−2)²+0²+2²+4²]/5 = 40/5 = 8, so standard deviation = √8 ≈ 2.828. CV = (2.828/14)×100 ≈ 20.2%. The other options result from incorrect calculations.

mcqs.question: Data set A = {50, 55, 60, 65, 70} and Data set B = {30, 45, 60, 75, 90}. Which data set is more consistent?

options.D: Consistency cannot be determined without more information

mcqs.explanation: For A, mean = 60, σ ≈ 7.07, CV ≈ 11.8%. For B, mean = 60, σ ≈ 21.21, CV ≈ 35.4%. The smaller CV indicates lower relative dispersion, so A is more consistent. Options B, C, D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Class X scored an average of 80 with a standard deviation of 8. Class Y scored an average of 50 with a standard deviation of 12. Which class shows greater relative dispersion?

options.C: Both have the same relative dispersion
options.D: Cannot be determined without the number of students

mcqs.explanation: CV_X = (8/80)×100 = 10%. CV_Y = (12/50)×100 = 24%. A higher CV means greater relative dispersion, so Class Y is more dispersed. Options A, C, D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the coefficient of variation (CV) is a common misconception?

options.A: CV is always expressed as a percentage.
options.B: CV is unit‑less and can be compared across different data sets.
options.D: CV can be used to compare relative variability of data sets with different units.

mcqs.explanation: The misconception is that CV cannot exceed 1 (or 100%). In reality, if the standard deviation is larger than the mean, CV can be greater than 100%. Options A, B and D are correct statements about CV.

mcqs.question: A data set has a mean of 200 and a variance of 400. What is its coefficient of variation?
mcqs.explanation: Standard deviation = √variance = √400 = 20. CV = (20/200)×100 = 10%. The other options arise from incorrect arithmetic.

mcqs.question: Data set P = {40, 45, 50, 55, 60} and Data set Q = {30, 40, 50, 60, 70} have the same mean. Which set is more consistent?

options.D: Consistency cannot be judged from the given information

mcqs.explanation: Mean of both sets = 50. For P, σ ≈ 7.07, CV ≈ 14.1%. For Q, σ ≈ 14.14, CV ≈ 28.3%. The smaller CV (P) indicates higher consistency. Options B, C, D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Two distributions have the same mean. Distribution A has a coefficient of variation of 12% and Distribution B has a coefficient of variation of 18%. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Distribution A is more relatively dispersed than Distribution B.
options.B: Distribution B is more relatively dispersed than Distribution A.
options.C: Both distributions have equal relative dispersion.
options.D: Coefficient of variation cannot be used to compare relative dispersion.

mcqs.answer: Distribution B is more relatively dispersed than Distribution A.
mcqs.explanation: A higher CV indicates greater relative dispersion. Since 18% > 12%, Distribution B is more dispersed. Option A reverses the relationship, C is false, and D is incorrect because CV is specifically designed for such comparisons.
